cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs a shell command by substituting user-controlled URL into a browser command template via path.replace("%u", href) and executes it via os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path]) without neutralizing shell metacharacters

connection.evidence: User-provided URLs from _goto(urls, fetch) are passed to _fork() where they are substituted into browser command template and executed via shell. The path from browser configuration contains the command template with %u placeholder.

diff_causality.evidence: This line calls _fork() but the vulnerable substitution and execution logic exists in the _fork function itself (lines 142-145). The candidate line enables the call chain but doesn't directly contain the injection mechanism.

security_control.evidence: No input validation or sanitization is applied to URLs before shell substitution
security_control.required_control: Shell metacharacter neutralization or parameterized execution
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-78 requires neutralization when user input is incorporated into shell commands to prevent command injection
existing_controls_checked: encoder() function applied to final command (line 143) but after substitution, not to URL input
No URL validation or shell escaping before substitution into %u placeholder
security_control.deficiency_evidence: URLs are directly substituted into command template without escaping shell metacharacters; encoder() only applies to final command string after injection opportunity exists

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary command execution is possible if attacker controls URL input and can inject shell metacharacters, allowing full system compromise

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the _fork() call would not execute, preventing the browser command execution entirely, but the vulnerable substitution mechanism in _fork() would remain present for other callers.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled URLs passed to _fork() without validation
Browser command template uses %u placeholder for URL substitution
Final command executed via /bin/sh -c without parameterization
No shell metacharacter escaping applied to URL before substitution
unresolved_facts: Whether browser configuration path is user-configurable and could contain malicious templates
Specific validation in URL input sources
Whether encoder() function provides any shell escaping
review_comment: User-provided URLs are directly substituted into browser command templates and executed via shell without escaping shell metacharacters. The _fork function replaces %u placeholders with raw URLs and passes the command to /bin/sh -c, allowing command injection if URLs contain shell metacharacters. Validate URLs against a safe pattern or use subprocess with argument lists instead of shell execution to prevent injection.
